---
title: "How do I calculate a confidence interval for a population mean?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I calculate a confidence interval for a population mean?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Verify the observations and whether a mean-based interval is sensible.

2. Set the desired confidence level.

3. Use t.test(x,conf.level=...) and report the estimated interval.

## Runnable example

```{r}
x <- c(11,12,14,15,17,18,19,20)
estimate <- t.test(x,conf.level=.95)
print(estimate$estimate)
print(estimate$conf.int)
```

## Interpret the result

The printed endpoints form a 95% confidence interval for the population mean under the test's assumptions. A wider interval usually indicates more uncertainty.

## Check before using real data

95% confidence describes the long-run coverage of the procedure, not a 95% probability about a fixed parameter after data are observed.
